I'm keeping a small margin and won't go lower, because GNSS and voice need a working 10-layer board. That still leaves the interior over by about 1134 mm³. I'm objecting because of the ledger overage, not my own numbers. The remaining cuts must come from battery, antenna, structure and acoustics. I'd rather see the wall thinned or the NFC and haptics volumes trimmed than lose board area. Each +0.1 mm of wall costs 150 mm³ for everyone.

Battery can give some volume, but runtime tracks cell volume at roughly 0.0158 h/mm³. Siren endurance also depends on battery energy, so I can't trade much away. I'm probing 3700, 3600 and 3500 mm³, with area set so thickness stays at or below 4.8 mm. The board stack is 4.73 + 2.24 = 6.97 mm, which is under the 7.1 mm limit. Smaller area also frees caseback plane for the thermal spreader.

Antenna: GNSS L5 is a priority, and 0.208 efficiency at 1500 mm³ is already low, so I can't cut blindly. I'm probing V_ant at 1300 and 1700 mm³, plus a thinner wall.

A thinner wall helps both of us. Titanium detunes the antenna less, and each -0.1 mm returns 150 mm³ to the interior pool. Going from 1.2 to 1.0 mm frees 300 mm³. Structure lead, please check whether 1.0-1.1 mm still meets your drop and pressure requirements.

NFC is counted once in the interior total. The perimeter has 580 mm³ of headroom, so it isn't the binding limit. I'll hold 1500 mm³ until the probes show the efficiency slope. I still OBJECT because of the interior overage.

Thermal: 320 mm² (250 mm³) gives exactly 43.0 °C at 1.2 mm wall and 0.9 W, so I have no slack to cut at the current wall. Spreader volume is small. Each +40 mm² costs only 31 mm³ and uses caseback plane, which the battery's smaller footprint frees up.

I'm probing whether wall thickness changes skin temperature, since structure may move it. If a thinner wall holds or improves temperature, I can accept it, and each -0.1 mm returns 150 mm³ to everyone. I'm also probing a larger spreader as margin. I still OBJECT because the interior is over by about 1,050 mm³, not because of my own numbers.

Structure: I can't thin the wall. At 1.2 mm, 9 mm² port and 1800 mm³ ribs, my pressure margin is 1.438, below the 1.5 requirement. So I'm objecting on my own numbers, not just the ledger overage.

I'm probing three ways to reach 1.5:
- More rib volume (2000 mm³).
- A thicker wall (1.3 mm). This costs everyone 150 mm³, so I'd rather avoid it.
- A smaller port (7 mm²). The port opening reduces margin, so this may be the cheapest fix. Acoustics, please say how much port reduction your 86 dB and voice targets can tolerate.

I'll report which option gives the most margin per mm³ next round. I'm not offering any volume cut until margin is fixed.

Acoustics: my siren fails. It needs 9.08 W against the 1.0 W limit, and at 3.72 Q the resonance sits at 5581 Hz. With the current battery that gives only 0.33 h of endurance, against the 3 h target. Voice SII is fine at 88.8, so I have room to trade for siren efficiency.

I'm moving the mesh to the 20 rayl floor and lengthening the outer port to pull the resonance down. I'm probing three variants:
- A: same volume and port, with the mesh and h_out changes.
- B: port 7 mm² with 1300 mm³. This answers Structure's port question.
- C: 1100 mm³ with a longer h_out.

I can likely give back 200-350 mm³ and some port area, depending on what the probes show. I won't claim a final cut until the siren number is credible. I OBJECT on my own siren requirement.

Haptics: force scales linearly with volume, about 0.00305 N/mm³ (1.069 N at 350 mm³). The 0.9 N floor is therefore 295 mm³. I'm cutting 350 to 310 mm³, which gives roughly 0.947 N, a 5% margin. That returns 40 mm³ to the pool. I'll go lower only if the others show the pool still failing and the probes confirm force at 300 mm³. I can't go below 295.

Haptics is a small slice, so the big savings must come from the wall, acoustics and antenna. I still OBJECT because the ledger is over by roughly 1,000 mm³, not because of my own numbers.

NFC: my read range is 18.2 mm against a 10 mm requirement, so I have real slack. GNSS and voice come first, and NFC will give volume to the pool.

- **This round:** I'm cutting from 500 to 380 mm³ (loop 240, ferrite 140), which returns 120 mm³.
- **Probes:** I'm testing the floor at 180/110 (290 mm³) and two intermediate points. If they hold at least 10 mm with margin, I'll go deeper next round, so Antenna can count on up to about 200 mm³ from me.

- **Ledger:** I still OBJECT because the ledger is over, not because of my own numbers.
